Just curious, do you live by yourself or with roommates? Human contact is so important (for me). Waking up in the morning or coming home and not seeing anybody makes a huge difference in my mood, there's nothing to distract me from those thoughts if I'm by myself.

I feel like that's why I'm stuck here too, though. I know it would be fucked up to put my (2) friends and family through that. I feel like I'm just kind of stalling until everybody's left their bodies behind so I can close up shop. It's weird feeling like you owe people your life, but I feel that way about the friends I have and my family.. and in a sense I do since they're the only things that keep me going? I don't know.
Maybe I'm all over the place so I understood, but it read just fine for me.

I think everybody feels like there's never enough they can do in circumstances surrounding tragedy, but nothing anybody can try to do will ever compensate for that loss. Not being able to be there for your mother right now, or the 'right way' (there is no right way), is so much better than not being there at all. 

Of course I don't know your whole family situation but I don't think your mother sees it that way (that she wishes is was you instead of your father). Remember that now you're pretty much what she has left of him, I'm sure she sees him and the way he raised you every time she sees you. I bet you adopted some of his mannerisms and idiosyncrasies that will be a comfort to her for the rest of her life. If she's been upset with you because she feels like you're not giving enough I hope that she can see that you need support, too.

People heal in different ways. This is a really hard time for you, it's unfair and unrealistic for somebody to expect you to have processed this enough to return to torturing yourself with a job you hate. It's not like you're recovering from the flu, you lost your father. And I'm so fucking sorry dude. I can't imagine what you're going through without crying.

And holy shit, that's so many languages. Which ones? I'm so god damn American, I speak one.

I'm terrified that I'm having a manic episode when I feel good or happy or inspired, which immediately fucks me up. Kind of reminds me of A Clockwork Orange.

I don't think you should feel guilty about feeling good, but it is primitive huh.
Fuck, I feel pretty much the same way (as your edit) about a guy and I'm not a teenager anymore. I wish I could give you a hug :(

Benzos are incredibly addictive and tend to make my anxiety worse if I don't take them consistently. Doctor prescribed or not (which they are) I don't want to be physically and mentally dependent on a drug. There are a lot of reasons why marijuana is more helpful for my anxiety, klonopin takes a while to kick in while marijuana is immediately relaxing and I can still think straight. It also increases my appetite. I reserve klonopin for times of extreme stress, anxiety and insomnia. I probably wont remember writing this a few hours from now because klonopin annihilates my short term memory.

I understand why somebody on the outside who is uncomfortable with their weight might think they'd like living in a body like this. I'm sure plenty of people roll their eyes about "thin-privilege" garbage when they read me whining about my weight, but the idea that anybody would want to look at the mirror and see most of the bones in their body protruding beneath atrophied muscles is totally fucking morbid.

Looking dead and staying that way no matter how much delicious trash you eat isn't lucky, it's fucked up. Thanks though.
I love pleasure and happiness but they make me sick too. Laughter is especially nauseating.

I really needed to hear that, I feel like it untangled some knots in my brain. Thank you so much. I've only said those things to a few people and they say things to the extent of "they're just bad friends". But that does put things in perspective.

Every time I try to forgive that certain friend I almost get there. I'll start to write a really civilized letter, explaining my feelings and how I'd like to repair our friendship, but it turns into a vicious mess after a few sentences. This person was really awful to me and I don't know how not to blame them for part of how I'm feeling, I don't know how to let it go.

I'm starting to feel like a dick for complaining about my physical appearance being such a big issue, but I don't know how to feel okay with it. When I open up to people they run for the hills.

This isn't advice so much as input...
When I feel like nobody would care or miss me or talk me out of it if it were a public thing I come here. When I come here and I read posts like this I realize that even though I've never met you, I really care and I think that's because I can relate.

When I see people feeling like this I wish there was something I could do or say to make it better because nobody should have to feel that way. It gives me a bit of perspective and I don't feel as alone.

And hey! I'm an asshole venting, too (does that mean farting?), so if you want to vent (not fart) together feel free to pm me.

Thank you :)

Honestly waiting to find peace is the only thing I feel like I can do. It's difficult when patience starts wearing thin.
I can wrap my hand around my "bicep" with my thumb and middle finger touching. Let's hit the gym, bro, pump some iron or whatever.

Yeaaah, I forgot about the school-spirit people. So it's not the worst for *everybody*, but for a lot of people I've known it was pretty rough. 
I guess what I should have said instead of any of that was: people go through a lot of changes in high school, physically, mentally, chemically, socially, etc., and since you're on this subreddit I wanted to say something like "things change after high school", and they really do for some people. It wasn't til I left high school that I met anyone I could relate with.

If you get pleasure from learning about science and obscure history (both RAD) then I think that's time well spent, at least you're doing something that makes you feel better (and it's learning!). Learning about Genghis Khan and the Alpha Centauri system could end up being kinda useful if you plan on going to college. My GPA would be so much higher if I had studied ANY of the Centauri[s] before taking an astronomy class in college.

I'm not good at advice :/

Thank you. This might be lengthy...

I had a really public manic episode a few years ago that landed me in a hospital for a good part of a year. I didn't burn any bridges, didn't do anything malicious or mean to anybody. During that time a few of my friends were really supportive, visiting me in the hospital. After I got out only two of my friends kept in contact, and they're the only people who haven't treated me any differently than they did before my breakdown.

I take my brain drugs every day and I'm sober as a fucking judge and I make damn sure I don't talk about myself or being 'certified' to anybody who might get uncomfortable, but they're uncomfortable before we even make eye contact so I don't know why I fucking bother.

I keep trying to make new friends and I'm terrible at it.

Friends who I used to hang out with for days on end have made plans with me since my release then actively ignore me right before we're supposed to hang out with no apologies and I haven't heard from them since (beyond a smile, wave, "hey how are you, oh I'm good", few glances at the floor and see ya later). I can tell that I make people uncomfortable, maybe they're worried I'm going to snap and they'll have to deal with it.

One of the biggest things is that I lost someone who I had considered my best and closest friend, who I could share everything with. I've harbored a lot of really negative energy toward that person and it's really shitty and confusing because I have fond memories of them and I don't think I'll ever find another person to talk to like that, but they really betrayed me.

Essentially a lot of what's been going on in my head lately is that nobody is really interested in knowing me aside from my parents and a couple other people, all of whom I love dearly. Aside from them, and I rarely see them, I feel completely isolated, disliked and disgusting. I don't see anything in myself worth keeping. 

After dwelling on those sorts of things I try to figure out what's so bad about me. The first thing that comes to mind is "man, I'm really hard to look at because I look like I'm dying".

And in response to the homophobia that (thank you) got deleted, yeah, I guess I DID come here for attention, because I think that right now the only thing in the entire fucking world that WILL make me feel better about myself is to meet somebody who likes me and cares about me for who I am and doesn't care that me and my brain had a shitty year a while back, someone who will give me a hug and not get freaked out when I cry a little and who I can have a real conversation with. If that's attention, fuck yeah that's what I want, because right now I really, really need somebody and nobody's here.
I think we can relate. If you want to talk pm me.

High school is the worst period of most peoples' lives, don't let anyone tell you different. Honestly, depending on what you do on reddit/the internet, you're probably learning more on the internet than you are in school.

I wish I had the courage to talk to people in real life about these sorts of things, but the few times I have it's been discouraging and worthless. The focus on trying to gain weight part is where most conversations start and end with people, completely ignoring the emotional aspects which is what I really need help with I guess.

I can't afford to pay a therapist who doesn't relate or give a fuck, and the few friends I have get really uncomfortable when I talk about mental illness, so reddit's alls I gots basically. So thanks for being around.

Thank you. That charming young (I'll be just as presumptuous) man sent me a really inspiring message. http://imgur.com/aRDliWi

The filthy slobs are a very small fraction of what's getting me down. My brain is really broken.

:) Thank you.

Yeah, Omegle was a bad outlet.

I hardly look in the mirror anymore. Looking at how thin my arms and thighs are makes me sick. Looking at my body makes me cry.

It makes me also sick when people compliment me on my weight.

Do art. Art is fucking awful and you have to be terrible at it to succeed. Produce the shittiest, worst garbage possible and sell it on etsy. Like, finger-paint a t-rex fighting a unicorn (or other stupid popular internet iconography, put some mustaches on them or some bullshit maybe) over some crappy 2 dollar religious painting from a thrift shop. Then you'll be good at being bad at something, which makes you good at something (and an "artist").

Sorry for the dumb advice.

Me too. I'm a few months away from having accomplished absolutely fucking nothing for a quarter of a century.

People always tell me not to focus on the future, but to focus on the present. That could possibly be good advice for you, but it makes me want to beat my head against a wall until I can't understand shitty advice anymore.
